jobs.title: Emergency Planning Officer
jobs.description:
About the role
As an Emergency Planning Officer, you will support the Service Manager in delivering the council’s emergency planning function and ensuring compliance with the Civil Contingencies Act 2004.

You will deputise for the manager in their absence and lead on emergency management training and project work to ensure the council is fully prepared for emergencies.

Key Responsibilities

Champion and advocate for emergency preparedness and resilience across the organisation, delivering training and helping build a diverse cohort of staff ready to support the council’s response to an emergency or major incident.
Proactively engage with the London Resilience Unit and other key partners to strengthen the council’s preparedness and contribute actively to London’s regional resilience work.
Contribute to maintaining the Borough Risk Register, incorporating national, regional and local risks, and actively horizon-scan for emerging threats.
Lead the development, improvement and maintenance of major incident and emergency plans to ensure the council can support statutory partners and the community during response and recovery.
Develop and maintain a risk-informed programme for reviewing, testing and validating emergency and major incident plans.
Maintain the council’s emergency management rota systems.
Assist the council with fulfilling its business continuity requirements.
Provide expert advice and guidance on emergency preparedness, including participating in testing or reviewing emergency plans for large-scale or high-risk events.
Build strong partnerships with external stakeholders, including London Resilience and other London boroughs, to share learning and improve preparedness.
Participate in the council’s response to and recovery from major incidents and emergencies, including out-of-hours and weekend work, acting as a resilience advisor to the command team and escalating risks appropriately.
Ensure Service Level Agreements (SLAs) are in place where required, with clear performance and response standards and escalation routes.
Ensure all purchasing and procurement complies with corporate guidelines and financial processes.
Organise and maintain the council’s Emergency Response arrangements, ensuring they remain effective, compliant with legal obligations, and aligned with best practice.
Horizon scan for lessons from emergencies and major incidents across the country, applying learning locally.
Identify and suggest improvements to ways of working to ensure an efficient and effective service for victims.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will need:

Detailed knowledge of emergency planning, business continuity, local government and the Civil Contingencies Act 2004.
Experience researching and developing plans and policies.
Experience building relationships at all levels internally and with external partners.
A high standard of education (e.g., a relevant degree) or significant experience in Emergency Planning & Business Continuity.

Why Join Us?

At Hillingdon, we are proud of our commitment to Putting Our Residents First , ensuring they remain at the heart of everything we do. We want to attract talented individuals who share this vision and can help us deliver exceptional services for the borough.

This is a full-time role (36 hours per week), with a minimum requirement of one day per week in the office (Uxbridge).

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
Aiviq is a fintech company transforming how asset managers globally process, analyse, and leverage their data. Our solutions power critical business processes for leading financial institutions worldwide, helping them drive efficiency and growth.

About the opportunity:

We are creating a new Customer Success Manager role, sitting alongside our Customer Services team and reporting directly to the Head of Operations. You will own the day-to-day health of our customer relationships, keep senior sponsors informed and confident, and make sure our customers are getting maximum business value from our cloud-based data and analytics platform.
You will be the person our customers trust to tell them what is really happening, and the person our internal teams turn to understand our customers needs and expectations. Sales will continue to own the commercial and contractual relationship; your focus is the growth, retention and satisfaction of our client base, through operational success, adoption and advocacy.
This is a foundational hire. You will be writing the playbook rather than inheriting one, backed by a leadership team that understands why this role matters, and early on you will be hands-on with planning, prioritisation and follow-through across multiple Aiviq teams.

What you will be doing:

Relationship and stakeholder management

Own the business and operational relationship across a portfolio of Investment Manager customers, acting as the primary channel for communications to and from senior sponsors and ensuring messages are timely, accurate and pitched at the right level.
Build and maintain customer success plans capturing each customer’s strategic objectives, use cases, stakeholders and measures of success.
Facilitate regular service and business reviews covering service performance, delivery progress, data quality trends and roadmap alignment.
Maintain a live view of customer health and stakeholder mapping, combining service metrics, engagement, adoption and sentiment so that emerging problems, sponsor changes and single points of dependency are spotted early.

Operational oversight and prioritisation

Own the view of relative priority across your portfolio: where Aiviq's attention is most needed, and why. Day-to-day ticket triage and resolution remain with the Head of Customer Services.
Work with the Heads of Operations, Customer Services, Professional Services and Product to agree how Aiviq's specialist capacity is allocated, arriving with a clear, evidenced recommendation.
Work with Professional Services project managers on in-flight implementations, supporting customer readiness and a clean transition into production.
Convene the right internal people to unblock issues and keep commitments visible, and feed recurring themes back into Product, Engineering and Operations as structured improvement opportunities.

Escalation and incident communications

Be the visible point of contact when there is a significant customer escalation, owning the customer-facing narrative from initial escalation through to closure, and knowing when to escalate internally.
Deliver clear, honest communications and coordinate the internal response, setting realistic expectations on both sides so that issues feel managed and controlled rather than chaotic.
Lead post-incident follow-up, including root cause summaries, remediation plans and the actions needed to rebuild confidence.

Product releases and adoption

Represent the customer voice in roadmap discussions and channel structured feedback into Product.
Stay ahead of the Aiviq roadmap and release schedule, understanding what each new capability means in practice for each of your customers.
Translate upcoming features into customer-specific benefits and build the case for adoption with the right stakeholders.
Drive release readiness with customers, covering communications, timing, enablement, testing and sign-off, then track adoption and intervene where value is not being realised.

Working with Sales

Partner closely with Sales, sharing intelligence on customer health, stakeholder changes, satisfaction and emerging needs, and supporting reference customers, case studies and advocacy where customers are willing.
Identify and qualify expansion signals, such as new use cases, teams, data sources or geographies, and hand them to Sales cleanly and early.

Building the function

Help define Customer Success at Aiviq: playbooks, health scoring, escalation protocols, review cadences and tooling.
Report on customer satisfaction, engagement and adoption to the Operations leadership team, championing the customer internally, constructively and with evidence.

What you will need:

Substantial experience in customer success, client service or account management within B2B SaaS, fintech or data, including personal ownership of a portfolio of enterprise customers.
A track record of trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, and the confidence to handle difficult conversations.
The seniority and self-direction to operate without a playbook and, initially, without a team, setting priorities that reflect both customer and Aiviq business value.
Experience in the asset or wealth management industry and with enterprise data platforms.
Excellent written and verbal communication, with the credibility to present to a senior sponsor, and strong negotiation and influencing skills applied as much internally as externally.
The ability to translate in both directions: technical detail into business meaning, and business need into something services and engineering teams can act on. You need not be an engineer, but you must be comfortable with data concepts and unafraid of detail.
Strong organisational skills to balance multiple customers, priorities and internal teams at once, with sound judgement on when to escalate, when to reassure and when to say no.

What we look for:

A passion for customer success and for building strong, long-lasting customer relationships
Calm under pressure. The kind of person whose presence lowers the temperature in the room
Confidence and credibility without ego. Trusted by senior customers, and keen to build something new
A collaborative mindset that embodies Aiviq's core values of collaboration, openness, innovation and respect, and an open mind that brings diversity of thought

How your success will be measured:

Customer satisfaction (CSAT) across your portfolio
Customer engagement and health scores, and adoption of new product releases
Quality and timeliness of escalation and incident communications
Customer retention and advocacy, and the quality of opportunities handed to Sales

What we offer:

The opportunity to define a new function, and a clear path towards leading it as we grow
Career growth in a collaborative, globally expanding fintech, with development support
Where of interest, opportunities to work from other global locations as our international teams grow

Based in London, with home-working flexibility, though we will expect you in the Aiviq office or at customer sites as required, including travel where the relationship calls for it. Aiviq is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in our workforce.

jobs.title: Information Security Governance and Compliance Analyst
jobs.description:
Great journeys start with great people

Here at LNER, we're shaping the future of rail on one of the UK's most iconic routes. From our high-speed Azuma fleet, redefining long-distance travel, to our next generation of trains, Serenza, this is a moment of real transformation for LNER. We're investing in cutting-edge technology, sustainability, and most importantly our people, to deliver outstanding experiences for our customers. There has never been a more exciting time to grow your career with LNER!

So, what exactly does our Information Security Governance and Compliance Analyst do?

LNER is adapting to ensure timely, accurate and focused support to protect against the growing cyber threat the company is facing. Over the next 12 months, the InfoSec team will be involved in several flag ship projects including those specifically coming through the East Cost Digital Programme and the introduction of the new CAF fleet. This is a truly exciting time for InfoSec at LNER.

We are therefore pleased to be recruiting for a new Information Security Governance, Risk & Assurance Analyst and are looking for someone with experience in the delivery of risk controls, governance processes, supplier assurances and compliance programmes. We also require a detailed knowledge of current and future legislation within the information security sector for UK rail.

The Analyst will provide essential support and input into the InfoSec supplier assurance process, managing the initial review to highlight risk or areas for further investigation. They will also support the risk management framework by reviewing the InfoSec risk register and facilitating the delivery of risk treatment plans within the agreed timescales. This would also extend to activities required to manage the ISO27001 Corrective Actions Log and collation and verification of the Continuous Improvement element of the ISO27001 Standard.

This role involves collaboration with all areas of the business to ensure any Information Security requirements in current and future projects is correctly identified and tasks assigned.
The role provides cover to facilitate delivery of ECDP Programme by supporting the Information Security team across various projects, both current and upcoming.

You'll also be involved in:
Supporting the LNER Information Security Assurance processes, gaining thorough knowledge of the current processes.
Guiding critical and key suppliers through the process providing concise, accurate reporting to the Information Security Governance, Risk & Assurance Manager for sign off and to the Information Security Manager as required.
Managing the treatment tasks/plans identified as requiring remediation through the Information Security Risk Register.
Working with identified risk owners across the business ensuring the ISO27001 Corrective Actions Log is correct and accurately reflects remediations and agreed delivery.
Supporting the Information Security Manager and Governance, Risk & Assurance Manager conducting security assessments through vulnerability testing and risk analysis as required.
Coordinating and supporting surveillance audits in support of maintaining LNER's ISO27001 compliant status.
Coordinating Information Security Policy review in line with an agreed timetable from the Information Security Compliance Manager.
Acting as a point of contact for Design Authority papers. Undertaking first review of Technical Impact Assessment papers submitted to Design Authority requiring Information Security review. Supporting business owners completing TIA's and High Level Concept papers completing the relevant sections.
Developing and carrying out information security plans, policies and procedures.
Coordinating reporting across the tools used for managing assurance and compliance ensuring reporting is accurate, timely and supports decision making.
Monitoring use of security products data encryption and other security products and procedures.
Responding to the business day-to-day information security requests and investigating routine security related incidents such as: malware detections, DLP violations, phishing emails, password compromises, general security information support.

What you'll need

Current experience in an information security role, ideally within risk, governance or assurance.
Working knowledge of common security controls (e.g. firewalls, endpoint protection, logging and monitoring, access management) and the ability to understand and assess their effectiveness.
An understanding of core security principles and control domains (access control, encryption, vulnerability and patch management, incident response, business continuity).
Ability to demonstrate and articulate knowledge of compliance with the ISO27001, PCI DSS, GDPR, NIS Directive, and other security Standards.
Experience using GRC platforms to manage risk registers, controls and assurance activities.
Experience identifying, assessing, documenting and tracking information security risks, including agreeing treatment plans and following up on remediation.
Experience reviewing supplier security questionnaires and evidence (e.g. SOC 2 reports, ISO certificates, penetration test summaries) and making risk-based judgements on their adequacy.
Recognised industry security certification such as CISMP, CompTIA Security+ or equivalent is desirable.
Experience in providing written and verbal presentations across all levels of a company.
Demonstrate their knowledge and understanding of basic financial/technical information.
You'll be an effective team player, experienced at dealing at all levels with effective influencing and negotiating skills.
Ability to form constructive and proactive working relationships at all levels with all stakeholders whether internal or external.
Hands on experience of problem-solving and ability to stay calm under pressure.
ITIL Foundation certification desirable.

You'll enjoy

Free travel on LNER, plus 75% off other companies' tickets (for you and your dependents).
Discounted international train tickets (after one year's service).
50% discount on LNER tickets for friends and family.
Generous pension scheme.
Annual cycle to work schemes/electric vehicle scheme.
Discount, savings and cashback scheme from top retailers.
Health and wellbeing schemes and discounts.
A host of training opportunities to help further your career.
Rewards and awards to recognise when you shine.

What you will be doing:

Relationship and stakeholder management

Own the business and operational relationship across a portfolio of Investment Manager customers, acting as the primary channel for communications to and from senior sponsors and ensuring messages are timely, accurate and pitched at the right level.
Build and maintain customer success plans capturing each customer’s strategic objectives, use cases, stakeholders and measures of success.
Facilitate regular service and business reviews covering service performance, delivery progress, data quality trends and roadmap alignment.
Maintain a live view of customer health and stakeholder mapping, combining service metrics, engagement, adoption and sentiment so that emerging problems, sponsor changes and single points of dependency are spotted early.

Operational oversight and prioritisation

Lead post-incident follow-up, including root cause summaries, remediation plans and the actions needed to rebuild confidence.
